title: QBR & Health Check - Celerity Labs
next_steps: Send month-by-month billing breakdown and token usage by route
Share updated SOC 2 + penetration test report and KMS integration notes
Schedule 90-min technical deep dive with SRE and infra teams (tentative: 2026-07-08)
Stakeholder pricing review with finance - provide committed Dedicated quote by 2026-07-07
action_items: Priya Nair: Compile detailed per-route cost breakdown and current batching config [due: 2026-07-02]
Lena Ortiz: Run 3 model latency benchmarks (hosted vs dedicated) with Celerity sample prompt set and share results [due: 2026-07-06]
Samir Patel: Draft Dedicated capacity proposal and 12-mo pricing options [due: 2026-07-07]
Elena Morales (Celerity): Share network diagram and VPC peering constraints for private deployment assessment [due: 2026-07-03]
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents over the last quarter, and roadmap alignment. Customer is evaluating transition from hosted to Dedicated or Private for cost predictability and data controls; they want benchmarked latency numbers and a clear pricing proposal. Action items include billing breakdown, bench tests, and security docs.
topics: Usage & cost trends; reliability incidents and mitigations; Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs; roadmap and upcoming model changes; SSO/KMS/audit log compliance; next steps and pricing
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, this is Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE for Celerity. we also have lena and priya. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Rajiv Kapoor: doing good, thanks. busy quarter but excited to dig in.
[00:12] Priya Nair: quick agenda, we'll review usage and cost, look at reliability incidents, then talk roadmap and next steps. feel free to interrupt.
[00:20] Dr. Maya Chen: sounds great. our main goal for today is to decide whether moving to Dedicated makes sense - also want to understand the cost delta and perf improvements.
[00:30] Lena Ortiz: perfect, we'll start with usage. over the last 90 days Celerity's token consumption grew ~38%, highest growth on the classification route and chat assist. most of the heavy tails are during business hours PST.
[00:44] Elena Morales: that matches our alerts - CPU on app frontends spiked, but it was autoscaled. the cost spike surprised finance though.
[00:52] Samir Patel: right, and from the billing side the per-token unit cost increased because you crossed into higher concurrency causing more generated tokens per session; also some routes are running models with higher context length.
[01:10] Rajiv Kapoor: can you break down which routes are highest cost? is the QA model eating most of it?
[01:15] Priya Nair: yes, classification and the long-context summarizer are top 3. we'll send a route-by-route breakdown after the call - that's an action item.
[01:26] Dr. Maya Chen: also interested in how prefix/KV caching might reduce cost for our chat flows, we've got a lot of repeated system prompts.
[01:33] Lena Ortiz: caching will help especially for repeated prefixes; we can tune TTLs and cache granularity. also batching config changes can reduce per-token cost without materially changing latency if done carefully. we'll include recommended config.
[01:47] Samir Patel: quick note on Dedicated - customers typically see 20-40% unit cost reduction for steady-state workloads with the right autoscale and batching, plus predictability. but it requires a commit and some infra setup.
[02:05] Rajiv Kapoor: what's the rough lift for Private VPC? our security team wants KMS in-region and no egress to public endpoints.
[02:12] Elena Morales: yes, for us encryption key residency is non-negotiable.
[02:16] Lena Ortiz: Private gives you control for KMS/HSM and VPC peering, we can support customer-managed KMS and provide audit logs. need network diagram to validate peering and NAT rules.
[02:29] Dr. Maya Chen: can you share your SOC2 report and recent pen test?
[02:33] Samir Patel: absolutely, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and the latest pentest summary. Priya will attach them to the follow up.
[02:40] Priya Nair: noted.
[02:43] Rajiv Kapoor: reliability - we saw two incidents in April and one in May where latency spiked for 8-12 minutes. can you explain root causes and mitigations?
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: yeah, incident in April was a burst that saturated a GPU pool due to a customer-side loop; our routing fallback kicked in but there was queueing. mitigation: we rolled out improved pre-warm logic and adjustable concurrency caps per customer, and added more aggressive autoscale thresholds. the May incident was network transient in a provider region.
[03:17] Elena Morales: is there an SLA for latency or only uptime?
[03:20] Samir Patel: Hosted has uptime SLAs; Dedicated options can include latency SLOs depending on tier. we'll include SLO examples in the proposal.
[03:28] Rajiv Kapoor: ok. for the benchmarks, can you run our prompt set? we want p95/99 numbers and token cost across hosted and Dedicated configurations.
[03:36] Lena Ortiz: yes, please share the prompt set and sample traffic shape. we'll run three scenarios: hosted standard, Dedicated with reserved GPU pool, and Dedicated with quantized model variant. we'll log latencies, throughput, and cost.
[03:50] Dr. Maya Chen: quantization - how much perf hit or quality regression should we expect?
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: depends on model family; typically quantization (8-bit/4-bit) yields 1-6% quality delta for many open models, with 20-40% inference cost reduction. we'll recommend candidate quantization profiles for your workload.
[04:09] Samir Patel: roadmap - Redwood plans kernel improvements and better KV cache routing later this quarter; some of that will reduce cold-start latencies. we'll flag planned changes that could affect your model choices.
[04:20] Rajiv Kapoor: any breaking changes or migrations to watch out for? we've been burned by model renames before.
[04:24] Priya Nair: no disruptive changes planned; model versions will be additive and we support pinning. we'll notify customers in advance and provide migration guides.
[04:33] Elena Morales: SSO - we want SCIM + SAML enforcement and RBAC scoped to environment. current setup is basic SAML.
[04:40] Samir Patel: we support SCIM + SAML and fine-grained RBAC on Dedicated/Private. that'll be in the security doc.
[04:47] Dr. Maya Chen: ok, next steps from our side: we'll pull the prompt set, send network diagram, and finance will review the projected spend.
[04:55] Samir Patel: perfect. recap: Redwood will send billing breakdown, SOC2 and pentest, and run benchmarks with your prompts. Samir will prepare Dedicated pricing. schedule deep dive for 2026-07-08 tentative.
[05:08] Rajiv Kapoor: thanks all, appreciate the clear items.
[05:11] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[05:15] (call ends)
